seoTitle: How to Create a Stripe Checkout Page
metaDescription: Set up a Stripe Checkout page: create a product, choose a pricing model, generate a payment link, and share or embed it. Includes what Stripe charges per transaction.
intro: Stripe's hosted Checkout is the fastest way to start taking payments without building a custom payment form or handling card data yourself. Instead of writing integration code, you create a product, generate a link, and Stripe hosts a secure page that handles Apple Pay, cards, and other payment methods for you. This guide follows the actual dashboard screens for creating a payment link end to end, from product setup to the shareable URL you hand to customers.
prerequisites: A Stripe account (test mode is fine to start)
The product name and price you want to charge, if you haven't already created the product in Stripe
costNote: Creating a payment link itself is free. Stripe charges its standard per-transaction processing fee on whatever comes through the link, and the rate depends on the payment method and the customer's country. Stripe's own pricing page has the current numbers for your region instead of a figure that would go stale here.

steps.heading: Start from your Stripe dashboard
steps.body: Log into your Stripe dashboard and you land on the Today overview, showing gross volume, USD balance, and payouts at a glance. Stripe surfaces setup recommendations directly on this page, including a prompt to "embed a payment form on your site or redirect to a Stripe-hosted page," which is exactly the Checkout flow this guide sets up. Your API keys are also visible here in test mode, useful later if you want to move beyond a simple link into a coded integration.

image.caption: The Stripe dashboard Today view, with balance figures, a setup recommendation to embed a payment form, and test API keys.

steps.heading: Create a payment link and add your product
steps.body: From Payment Links, click the button to start a new link and choose Payment link. Stripe asks which pricing model you want first: Products or subscriptions for a fixed price, or Customers choose what to pay for donations and pay-what-you-want amounts. This guide follows the fixed-price path, which covers most product and subscription sales. On the Payment page tab, add your product — either an existing one from your catalog or a new one created on the spot with a name and price. In the example, an $11.00/year subscription product called "WP Domain Setup & Theme" is added with its tax code and quantity settings, and a live preview of the checkout page updates on the right as you configure it. Watch that preview closely: it shows exactly what the customer will see, including which payment methods (card, Apple Pay, Klarna, bank account) appear as options.

image.caption: Building a payment link for a subscription product, with a live preview of the hosted checkout page showing Apple Pay and card fields.

steps.heading: Configure the payment page options
steps.body: Below the product, Stripe gives you toggles for collecting tax automatically, collecting customer addresses, requiring a phone number, and offering a free trial on subscriptions. Turn on only what you need; every extra required field is one more chance for a customer to abandon checkout. If your product needs tax collected by jurisdiction, enable Collect tax automatically instead of trying to bake tax into the listed price by hand. The same settings area also has options for promotion codes and optional upsell items, worth a look if you sell add-ons alongside the main product.

steps.heading: Generate the link
steps.body: Click Create link and Stripe generates a live URL, by default on the buy.stripe.com domain or your own connected domain if you've set one up. This is your finished Checkout page; no separate hosting or embedding required to start using it. Adaptive Pricing is on by default for every payment link too, so a customer in another country sees the price converted into their local currency automatically. The link works immediately: anyone who opens it lands on the page you previewed, ready to pay.

image.caption: A completed payment link for the $11.00/year product, showing the shareable URL, the product it's tied to, and enabled payment methods.

steps.heading: Share the link or embed it on your site
steps.body: The payment link's details page gives you more than the URL. There's a QR code you can download as a PNG, a Buy button snippet for embedding on your site, and options for adding URL parameters. Paste the plain link into an email, a social post, or a button on your site, or use the QR code for print materials. Either way, Stripe hosts the actual payment page, so PCI compliance work doesn't fall on your own server.

steps.heading: Verify payment methods before going live
steps.body: Check the Payment methods section under the link for which options are enabled. The example shows Card, Apple Pay, Klarna, Link, ACH direct debit, Cash App Pay, and Amazon Pay all switched on. Some of these need to be enabled separately in your account's payment method settings before they show up at checkout, so test the link once in test mode before sharing it publicly.

troubleshooting.problem: A payment method you expected doesn't show up at checkout
troubleshooting.cause: Some payment methods need to be turned on separately in your Stripe account's payment method settings before they appear on any link.
troubleshooting.fix: Go to Settings > Payment methods in the Dashboard, enable the method, then reload the link's preview to confirm it shows up.

troubleshooting.problem: A bank-debit or voucher payment doesn't complete right away
troubleshooting.cause: Some payment methods take between 2 and 14 days to confirm, so the payment isn't marked complete the moment a customer submits the form.
troubleshooting.fix: Set up a webhook for the payment-succeeded event instead of assuming payment finished as soon as the customer clicked through.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no way to delete an old payment link
troubleshooting.cause: Stripe payment links can't be deleted once created, only deactivated.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the overflow menu on the link and choose Deactivate. The URL then redirects to an expiry page instead of the checkout page.

faq.question: Do I need coding skills to set up Stripe Checkout?
faq.answer: No. A payment link, as shown in this guide, is created entirely from the Stripe dashboard. Coding is only needed for a custom checkout session embedded through the API instead of a hosted link.

faq.question: Can I customize the look of the checkout page?
faq.answer: Within limits. Stripe offers 20 preset fonts, a handful of border-radius options, and lets you set your own logo, background, and button colors. You can also connect your own domain so the page doesn't show buy.stripe.com.

faq.question: Does Stripe Checkout support multiple products?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Add another product on the payment link builder to include more items (Stripe allows up to 20 line items on a single link), and let customers adjust quantity where that's supported.

faq.question: Is Stripe Checkout secure for customers?
faq.answer: Yes. Stripe Checkout is a hosted, PCI-compliant page, so card details are entered directly on Stripe's domain and never pass through your own server.

faq.question: Can I delete a payment link once it's created?
faq.answer: No. Payment links can't be deleted, only deactivated. Deactivating stops new purchases immediately, and reactivating it later brings the same URL back to life.

faq.question: Will customers see prices in their own currency?
faq.answer: Yes, by default. Adaptive Pricing is on for every payment link, so Stripe automatically converts and displays the price in the shopper's local currency.
